properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-25, dev_reflow2 hub session:

"say that I stop using the reflow2 local server and switch to the reflow2 mcp on api.flo2.io. Now say I cd to reflow2 for instance (which has the reflow2 design in the repo), will it try to rebuild the reflow2 design in the remote reflow2 mcp?"

CHECKED THE SAME EVENING, SO THIS STARTS FROM FACTS:
- NOTHING REBUILDS A DESIGN BY ITSELF. The repo's committed export (docs/design/reflow2.json) reaches a store only through an explicit import (`reflow2-mcp --import`, or the import_graph tool). Importing into an EMPTY store is a restore: same design, same name (main.rs).
- 🛑 BUT ONE PATH WOULD REBUILD IT, BY INSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY CODE. The SessionStart nudge (tools/loop_nudge.py) tells the agent: "call open_questions — if this design is empty, start it with the genesis skill (new project) or the adopt skill (code that already exists)". Pointed at a remote design that has not been moved yet, an agent in the reflow2 folder would see an empty design next to a large existing codebase and run ADOPT: reading the code back into a thin design with no decisions, no history and no rationale, while the real design sits unread in docs/design/reflow2.json. It would look like success.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

(a) MOVE IT ONCE, BY IMPORT. The committed export is the whole design, history included. Import it into the new remote design once; that is a restore and keeps the design's identity. Then write the pointer file (dec:idea-a-checkout-knows-which-remote-design-it-implements) and freeze the local store. It is flo2's "upload a design export" (flo2's dec:idea-bring-a-local-design-into-flo2, plan step 3), seen from the repo side. CHEAP; the import already exists.

(b) THE EMPTY-DESIGN NUDGE LEARNS THE DIFFERENCE. Before it offers genesis or adopt, it checks whether this folder already holds a design: a committed export or a local store. If it does, it offers "move this design" (a) and never adopt. SMALL, and it closes the one path that would rebuild.

(c) KEEP BOTH COPIES AND SYNC THEM. Recorded so it is not mistaken for unconsidered: two live copies need a rule for which wins, and flo2 already declined sync-rather-than-serve (option e of flo2's dec:idea-api-flo2-io-hosts-the-graph-for-a-local-agent).

AFTER THE MOVE, WHICH WAY THINGS FLOW:
- The remote design is THE design. (WITHDRAWN 2026-09-27: this line went on to say the repo's docs/design/reflow2.json "becomes a copy the local client writes back into the working tree (req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url, point 3), so the CI design gate still reads it". Rule 3 of dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy makes an export a copy that nothing tracks, so no client keeps one current. The CI gate moves to the server instead: req:ci-checks-the-code-against-its-design-on-the-server.)
- Repo → remote never happens by itself, only as a deliberate restore.
- A folder with BOTH a live local store and a pointer to a remote design is ambiguous. The client should refuse or warn rather than pick.

═══ PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══
· reflow2's OWN DESIGN MAY BE THE LAST ONE TO MOVE, NOT THE FIRST. It is the largest (5,495 nodes, 35,716 edges, a 23 MB export), and its workflow is built around a local store: per-worktree branch facts (req:implementation-facts-travel-with-the-branch-that-produced-them), one export per PR, and a release cut that exports from the new binary. Each of those has to work through the remote client first. cure, which has no such history, is the natural first case.
· THE EXPORT CHAIN MUST SURVIVE THE MOVE. Each committed export records the hash of the one before it. The first export written back after the move has to chain from the repo's last committed one, or the gate sees a break. That the import keeps it is expected, not yet checked.
· req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine stands: moving is a choice per design, and nothing here makes it happen by default.

═══ SETTLED 2026-09-25 BY ANTHONY: (a) AND (b); cure MOVES FIRST. (c) NOT CHOSEN ═══
Anthony: "keep (a) and (b), cure moves first".
- (a) A repo's design moves to a remote server once, by importing its committed export (a restore that keeps the design's identity), then the pointer file is written and the local store is frozen.
- (b) The empty-design nudge checks whether the folder already holds a design (a committed export or a local store) and offers the move, never adopt.
- cure is the first design to move. reflow2's own design moves later, once its branch, export-per-PR and release-cut workflow work through the remote client.

═══ 2026-09-26 — cure MOVED; flo2 AND reflow2 HELD UNTIL THE LOCAL CLIENT EXISTS ═══
cure moved to flo2.io this day by exactly (a): its export imported into an empty store on the droplet (identity 54ae4a4f0b458b77 kept, 115 nodes, 276 edges), the owner recorded, the laptop store frozen with a note in its folder. Anthony then asked to move all three; the move of flo2's and reflow2's own designs was HELD on his word ("Yes, hold flo2 and reflow2 until the local client is built"), because both repositories' workflows need a local design today: the CI design gate reads the committed export, every PR re-exports into the working tree, artifact registration and drift checks measure local files, and a release cut freezes local checksums. api.flo2.io refuses the file-facing tools, so until reflow2's local client (req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url) writes the export locally and measures local files, moving either would stop their PRs and releases. Order: the local client, then flo2, then reflow2.

═══ 2026-09-27 — WHAT THE HOLD NOW WAITS FOR ═══
The hold on flo2's and reflow2's own designs stands, but what ends it has changed. Under the design-and-export rules the client will not write the export locally. The hold now ends at step 8 of the tracked-export retirement plan (epoch:planned-flo2-then-reflow2-move-and-the-photocopy-retires), once CI checks code against the design on the server (step 6) and a release cut works against a remote design (step 7). The order flo2 first, then reflow2, is unchanged. cure's frozen laptop store was deleted on Anthony's word the same day.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-09-25 — a repo's design moves to a remote server once, by import; the empty-design nudge offers the move and never adopt; cure moves first
